text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A cargo of 20,000 tonnes of petrol will arrive in Lagos on Monday, but marketing companies say the quantity will not be enough to ease the fuel shortage which has hit Nigeria.
- The Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission, designed to encourage direct foreign investment, will soon be inaugurated by government.
- Speculative trading is to blame for big falls in the prices of several blue chip shares trading on the Nigerian Stock Exchange.

- Healthy banks have initiated measures to consolidate their positions in the wake of a clampdown on distressed banks. Measures include intensive advertising, opening new branches and quicker service delivery.
- Central bank approves universal banking to start from January 1999. Commercial and merchant banks will be free to provide the same services instead of being forced to specialise.
- Manager of southern Warri oil refinery says Nigeria's current fuel shortage may be traced to recent violent protests in the area which have hampered distribution of products from the refinery.
- The Presidency may have stopped the closure of the London office of Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation, pending investigation of alleged secret bank accounts.

- Relations of those who died in the November ADC airlines crash will receive at least $25,000 from the plane's insurers for each victim. Those in higher socio-economic groups will receive up to $50,000. All 132 people on board the Boeing 727 died when it crashed into a lagoon near Lagos.
